members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the alignment acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body in TwoAttachment mode (measured: OneAttachment needs Attachment0 alone). Read only.

members.name: AlignType
members.summary: What turns: AllAxes (the default) the whole orientation; PrimaryAxisParallel Attachment0's X parallel to the goal's X; PrimaryAxisLookAt Attachment0's X toward LookAtPosition (one attachment) or Attachment1's position (two). Parallel, Perpendicular and PrimaryAxisPerpendicular are refused (a recorded divergence).

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The goal orientation in OneAttachment mode: Attachment0 turns to its rotation; its translation is saved and ignored, as the reference's (a look-at aims at LookAtPosition). Default identity.

members.name: LookAtPosition
members.summary: The world point Attachment0's X turns toward when AlignType is PrimaryAxisLookAt and Mode is OneAttachment. Neither saved nor replicated: a client's is its own. Default (0, 0, 0).

members.name: MaxAngularVelocity
members.summary: The speed Attachment0 turns toward its goal at, at most, in radians per second. Default inf.

members.name: MaxTorque
members.summary: The most torque the alignment turns with; math.huge is no limit. Default 10000.

members.name: Mode
members.summary: TwoAttachment (the default) turns Attachment0 to Attachment1's orientation; OneAttachment turns it to CFrame's.

members.name: PrimaryAxis
members.summary: The goal's X axis in OneAttachment mode — a view of CFrame's rotation: a write turns the goal so its X is the axis, keeping its Y as near as perpendicularity allows. Default (1, 0, 0).

members.name: PrimaryAxisOnly
members.summary: Deprecated on the reference: set AlignType instead. True makes AllAxes turn the primary axes alone, as PrimaryAxisParallel does. Default false.

members.name: ReactionTorqueEnabled
members.summary: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite torque (TwoAttachment mode). Default false.

members.name: Responsiveness
members.summary: How quickly Attachment0 turns to its goal: an approach without overshoot that settles in about 13 / Responsiveness seconds (45 is within 1 degree of a quarter turn at 0.32 s, measured). Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end (measured), an infinite one included; a NaN write is refused. Default 10.

members.name: RigidityEnabled
members.summary: Always false: the rigid alignment is not built, and a write of true is refused (a recorded divergence).

members.name: SecondaryAxis
members.summary: The goal's Y axis in OneAttachment mode — a view of CFrame's rotation: a write turns the goal about its X toward the axis. Default (0, 1, 0).

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Draws the editor's marker for the alignment whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

classes.name: AlignOrientation
classes.summary: A mover: a torque that turns Attachment0 to Attachment1's orientation, or to CFrame's with one attachment — the whole orientation, its primary axis alone, or that axis toward a point (AlignType; LookAtPosition with one attachment) — as quickly as Responsiveness asks and within MaxTorque and MaxAngularVelocity.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the alignment acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body in TwoAttachment mode or when the per-axis limit is in its frame (measured: OneAttachment needs Attachment0 alone). Read only.

members.name: ApplyAtCenterOfMass
members.summary: Whether the force acts at the assembly's centre of mass instead of at Attachment0. Default false.

members.name: ForceLimitMode
members.summary: Magnitude (the default) holds the force's length to MaxForce; PerAxis holds each axis of ForceRelativeTo's frame to its lane of MaxAxesForce.

members.name: ForceRelativeTo
members.summary: The frame whose axes the PerAxis limit applies along: the world's (the default), Attachment0's or Attachment1's.

members.name: MaxAxesForce
members.summary: The most force along each axis of ForceRelativeTo's frame under the PerAxis limit; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (10000, 10000, 10000).

members.name: MaxForce
members.summary: The most force the alignment pushes with under the Magnitude limit — the assembly's weight included; math.huge is no limit. Default 10000.

members.name: MaxVelocity
members.summary: The speed Attachment0 approaches its goal at, at most, in studs per second (measured as an exact cap). Default inf.

members.name: Mode
members.summary: TwoAttachment (the default) carries Attachment0 to Attachment1; OneAttachment carries it to Position.

members.name: Position
members.summary: The goal in world space in OneAttachment mode: Attachment0 is carried there. Default (0, 0, 0).

members.name: ReactionForceEnabled
members.summary: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite force (TwoAttachment mode). Default false.

members.name: Responsiveness
members.summary: How quickly Attachment0 reaches its goal: an approach without overshoot that settles in about 13 / Responsiveness seconds (45 is within 0.1 stud of a 10-stud goal at 0.32 s, measured). Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end (measured), an infinite one included; a NaN write is refused. Default 10.

members.name: RigidityEnabled
members.summary: Always false: the rigid alignment is not built, and a write of true is refused (a recorded divergence).

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Draws the editor's marker for the alignment whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

classes.name: AlignPosition
classes.summary: A mover: a force that carries Attachment0 to Attachment1, or to Position with one attachment, as quickly as Responsiveness asks and within MaxForce and MaxVelocity — holding the assembly's weight while it does.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the angular velocity target acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it; the fresh zero MaxTorque leaves it active (measured). Read only.

members.name: AngularVelocity
members.summary: The angular velocity, radians per second, the torque brings Attachment0's assembly to within each physics step, in RelativeTo's frame — relative to Attachment1's assembly under Attachment1. Default (0, 0, 0).

members.name: MaxTorque
members.summary: The most torque the target spins the assembly with; the default 0 turns nothing, as does any value of 0 or less (the hinge's rule); math.huge is no limit.

members.name: ReactionTorqueEnabled
members.summary: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite torque — with RelativeTo Attachment1, the frame it is meaningful in. Default false.

members.name: RelativeTo
members.summary: The frame AngularVelocity is named in: the world's (the default), Attachment0's, or Attachment1's — the spin then relative to Attachment1's assembly.

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Draws the editor's marker for the angular velocity target whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

classes.name: AngularVelocity
classes.summary: A mover: a torque that brings Attachment0's assembly to an angular velocity within each physics step, named in RelativeTo's frame, within MaxTorque — whose default 0 turns nothing.

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The attachment's LOCAL pose relative to its parent part (§15); the world-space view is WorldCFrame.

members.name: Orientation
members.summary: The attachment's LOCAL rotation as YXZ Euler angles in degrees: (rx, ry, rz) names the product Ry·Rx·Rz, where CFrame.Angles composes Rx·Ry·Rz (§30).

members.name: Position
members.summary: The attachment's LOCAL position, relative to its parent part (§15). The world-space view is WorldPosition.

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Draws the editor's marker gizmo at the attachment's world pose. Purely an authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it.

members.name: WorldCFrame
members.summary: The attachment's world pose: the parent part's pose composed with the local CFrame — the local values when no posed parent exists. Writing it recomputes the LOCAL pose against the current parent (§15).

members.name: WorldPosition
members.summary: The attachment's world position (parent pose ∘ local). Writing it recomputes the LOCAL position against the current parent (§15).

classes.name: Attachment
classes.summary: A named point on a part: its CFrame, Position and Orientation are LOCAL to the parent, and the WorldCFrame/WorldPosition pair is the composed world view (writing it recomputes the local). Constraints anchor to attachments; Visible draws the editor marker.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the ball socket acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored (an anchored end leaves it active). Read only.

members.name: LimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether Attachment1's X axis stops hard within UpperAngle of Attachment0's — the tilt cone (measured a hard limit) — and, with TwistLimitsEnabled, its twist within the twist range. Default false.

members.name: MaxFrictionTorque
members.summary: The socket's friction torque. Reads 0, the default; a write of any other value is refused: the reference's friction holds the attachments' angle against a smaller load (measured) and the engine's solver has no such hold (not supported in v1).

members.name: Radius
members.summary: The size of the ball socket's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.15.

members.name: Restitution
members.summary: The cone's bounce, clamped to 0..1 at the write (measured), an infinity included; a NaN write is refused. Stored and saved, but inert: the socket stops dead at its limits whatever it holds (a recorded divergence, as the hinge's). Default 0.

members.name: TwistLimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the twist — the angle from Attachment0's Y axis to Attachment1's about their X — stops hard within TwistLowerAngle and TwistUpperAngle. One of the limits: it acts while LimitsEnabled is on too. Default false.

members.name: TwistLowerAngle
members.summary: The twist's lower limit in degrees, while TwistLimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write (measured), an infinity included; never reordered against TwistUpperAngle (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default -45.

members.name: TwistUpperAngle
members.summary: The twist's upper limit in degrees, while TwistLimitsEnabled (a 20 rad/s twist under ±10 stopped at 12.1 — measured). Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included, never reordered against TwistLowerAngle (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

members.name: UpperAngle
members.summary: The tilt cone's half angle in degrees, while LimitsEnabled: the most Attachment1's X axis turns from Attachment0's (a hung arm pushed hard stopped at 30.9 under 30 — measured). Clamped to 0..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

classes.name: BallSocketConstraint
classes.summary: A ball and socket: the two attachments held at one point, free to turn about it — while LimitsEnabled, Attachment1's X axis within UpperAngle of Attachment0's (a hard stop, measured), and with TwistLimitsEnabled its twist within TwistLowerAngle and TwistUpperAngle.

members.name: Anchored
members.summary: Whether the part is pinned in place. Anchored parts never simulate — no gravity, no forces — but still collide and fire Touched.

members.name: ApplyAngularImpulse
members.summary: Instant spin change on the assembly's body: the angular impulse in world axes through the assembly's inertia (delta-omega = I⁻¹ · impulse). Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored assemblies.

members.name: ApplyImpulse
members.summary: Instant velocity change on the assembly's body: delta-v equals impulse divided by the assembly mass. Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored (infinite-mass) assemblies.

members.name: ApplyImpulseAtPosition
members.summary: An impulse applied at a world position: the linear change of ApplyImpulse plus the spin its torque arm from the assembly's center of mass gives ((position - center) × impulse). Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored assemblies.

members.name: AssemblyAngularVelocity
members.summary: The assembly's angular velocity in radians per second about the world axes — welded members answer, and set, their assembly root's. A write reads back at once; on an anchored assembly it lands in the property and the solver ignores it.

members.name: AssemblyCenterOfMass
members.summary: The assembly's center of mass in WORLD space: the mass-weighted center of every welded member, carried by the root's pose. Read only.

members.name: AssemblyLinearVelocity
members.summary: The assembly's linear velocity — welded members answer their assembly root's. Reads are zero without a live body; writes on anchored parts land but the solver ignores them.

members.name: AssemblyMass
members.summary: The whole assembly's mass, every welded member's own summed; infinity for an anchored assembly. Read only.

members.name: BrickColor
members.summary: The nearest BrickColor of the part's Color (the rule of BrickColor.new(color)); a write stores the table colour's bytes as Color3.fromRGB would, so Color reads back equal to fromRGB of them — an ulp off the BrickColor's own Color, as measured. Every real change of the colour fires Changed("BrickColor") and the BrickColor property signal before Color's pair; the same value again fires nothing. A BrickColor only.

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The full rigid transform as one CFrame. Reads and writes agree with Position and Rotation — three views of the same pose. Welded members refuse the write; move the assembly root instead.

members.name: CanCollide
members.summary: Whether the part responds to contacts. false keeps it physical — it falls and fires Touched — but removes the contact response.

members.name: CastShadow
members.summary: Whether the part casts a shadow (true by default), under the sun and under a PointLight or SpotLight whose Shadows is on. A part that casts none still receives the shadows of others. A server's write replicates like any other property's.

members.name: CenterOfMass
members.summary: The part's own center of mass in its LOCAL frame — the origin for every symmetric shape. Read only.

members.name: Color
members.summary: The authored surface color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

members.name: GetMass
members.summary: The part's own mass — the Mass property as a method.

members.name: GetNetworkOwner
members.summary: Server-only: the player currently simulating this assembly, or nil for the server. Resolved through the assembly root.

members.name: GetNetworkOwnershipAuto
members.summary: Server-only: whether automatic (distance-based) ownership is in effect for this assembly.

members.name: GetRenderCFrame
members.summary: The world pose the part is DRAWN at this frame, which differs from CFrame while the render departs from the simulation under server authority: a correction's offset decaying, or a tick mover shown one tick behind (net-sync-v2 §2.9). A camera or an effect that must sit on what is on screen reads this in the render step; game logic reads CFrame.

members.name: Locked
members.summary: Whether the editor's viewport leaves the part alone: a click does not select a locked part and a box does not take it (the Explorer still selects it). Nothing at run time reads it; a server's write replicates like any other property's.

members.name: Mass
members.summary: The part's own mass: its material's density (the reference's numbers — Plastic 0.7, Metal 7.85, …) times its shape's volume. Read only.

members.name: Material
members.summary: The surface material, as an Enum.Material item; writes accept the item or its string name.

members.name: Position
members.summary: The part's world position. Welded members read their world pose, and a write moves the whole assembly with offsets preserved. Explicit writes fire the pose property signals; physics motion does not.

members.name: RotVelocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the assembly's angular velocity in radians per second about the world axes — use AssemblyAngularVelocity. A write sets it and keeps the velocity of the assembly root part's position (measured), where an AssemblyAngularVelocity write keeps the centre of mass's.

members.name: Rotation
members.summary: The orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees. Welded members read their assembly pose; writing a welded member is refused — rotate the assembly root instead.

members.name: SetNetworkOwner
members.summary: Server-only: pins which peer simulates this assembly (nil means the server) and turns automatic ownership off. A non-Player instance degrades silently to the server. The part must be an unanchored workspace descendant.

members.name: SetNetworkOwnershipAuto
members.summary: Server-only: re-arms automatic (distance-based) ownership without clearing the standing owner.

members.name: Size
members.summary: The part's dimensions in studs. The collider and mesh re-derive on write; a MeshPart's geometry scales against its authored MeshSize.

members.name: Touched
members.summary: Fires when another collider starts touching this part, with the other object. Exists on unparented parts too; fires once per contact start.

members.name: Transparency
members.summary: How see-through the part renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

members.name: Velocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the velocity of the part's own position — the assembly's linear velocity plus its spin's arm from the centre of mass (measured) — use AssemblyLinearVelocity. A write on any part of an assembly sets the velocity of the assembly root part's position, the spin kept; on a part alone the pair is the assembly's. Not signal-backed (the reference fires Changed; recorded).

classes.name: BasePart
classes.summary: Everything physical: world pose (Position, Rotation, CFrame), Size, appearance (Color, Material, Transparency), collision flags, and the Touched signal.

classes.name: BasePlayerGui
classes.summary: The per-player UI container layer; no members of its own here.

classes.name: BaseRemoteEvent
classes.summary: The remote-event layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

members.name: Disabled
members.summary: The legacy inverse of Enabled — the two always mirror each other.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: The script's run switch. Disabling kills the script's threads and listeners before the next pass; re-enabling restarts it fresh from the top. Writes require a real boolean (the reference engine coerces — a recorded strict-typing divergence).

members.name: RunContext
members.summary: Where the script runs: Legacy (placement decides), Server, or Client. Writes accept the enum item or its name string and re-derive execution immediately. A LocalScript's stored value is inert — its class decides.

classes.name: BaseScript
classes.summary: The runnable scripts: the Enabled/Disabled run switch and RunContext, which decides where the code executes.

members.name: AnchorPoint
members.summary: Which point of the billboard (0..1 per axis) its Position pins. A Vector2, like every GuiObject's.

members.name: Position
members.summary: The billboard's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

members.name: Size
members.summary: The billboard's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

classes.name: BillboardGui
classes.summary: A world-anchored UI root: its elements render at its parent's position, facing the camera.

members.name: Event
members.summary: The receiving side of Fire: listeners get the fired arguments. Delivery is deferred to the next script pass; arguments pass by reference within the shared VM (the reference engine deep-copies — a recorded divergence).

members.name: Fire
members.summary: Queues Event with these arguments for every listener, delivered on the next script pass.

classes.name: BindableEvent
classes.summary: A same-context signal object: Fire queues Event for every listener — script-to-script signaling without the network.

members.name: Invoke
members.summary: Calls OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results (multiple returns pass through). Errors when OnInvoke is unset (the reference engine blocks forever — a recorded divergence).

members.name: OnInvoke
members.summary: The handler Invoke calls. Assign a function or nil; unset reads nil, and calling Invoke while unset errors.

classes.name: BindableFunction
classes.summary: A same-context call object: Invoke runs the assigned OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results.

members.name: Value
members.summary: The stored boolean. Writes require a real boolean.

classes.name: BoolValue
classes.summary: A named container for one boolean.

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The eye's pose. Live in Custom — the orbit writes it every frame, and a script write re-seats the orbit from the written look direction at the current zoom (measured); authoritative in Scriptable. A script write fires the CFrame signal; the eye's own motion never does.

members.name: CameraSubject
members.summary: What the following modes track: any instance, though only one with a world pose (a part, a model, a character) or a Humanoid (followed through its body) moves the eye. The default is the local player's character's Humanoid (measured), and a nil write changes nothing — whatever subject was in place stays (measured).

members.name: CameraType
members.summary: Who drives the camera. Custom (the play default) and Track are the built-in orbit around CameraSubject; Follow is that orbit swinging behind the subject's movement; Orbital the orbit at a locked zoom that ignores CFrame writes; Attach rides the subject and turns with it; Watch stays put and turns to face it; Fixed stays exactly where scripts put it and leaves Focus alone; Scriptable obeys CFrame writes and nothing else. Writes accept the item or its name.

members.name: DiagonalFieldOfView
members.summary: The view across the viewport's diagonal, derived from FieldOfView and the viewport aspect by the reference engine's measured relation (tan(d/2) = tan²(v/2) + tan²(h/2)); a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

members.name: FieldOfView
members.summary: The VERTICAL field of view in degrees, clamped 1..120 (measured: 500 reads back 120, 0 reads back 1); default 70. A write fires this name and the two derived views.

members.name: FieldOfViewMode
members.summary: Which view a viewport resize preserves — Vertical (the default: FieldOfView itself), Diagonal or MaxAxis — with the vertical recomputed to keep it. FieldOfView always reads the vertical value whatever the mode (measured).

members.name: Focus
members.summary: The point of interest. The eye keeps it on the subject in every following mode (identity rotation), twenty studs ahead of the eye in Scriptable — where a script's own write is overridden the next frame (measured) — and untouched in Fixed.

members.name: GetPartsObscuringTarget
members.summary: Every part between the camera's position and any of the cast points — visible or not, collidable or not, the part around the point included — minus the ignore list with its descendants and the local player's character (measured); each part once.

members.name: GetRenderCFrame
members.summary: The pose the eye actually renders from — the camera's CFrame (the two differ only under VR head tracking).

members.name: HeadLocked
members.summary: Whether VR head tracking follows the camera (default true). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

members.name: HeadScale
members.summary: The VR head-to-world scale (default 1). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

members.name: MaxAxisFieldOfView
members.summary: The view along the viewport's larger axis — horizontal in landscape, the vertical itself in portrait; a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

members.name: NearPlaneZ
members.summary: The near clipping plane's z in the camera's own space: the negated near distance (−0.1).

members.decl: (x: number, y: number, depth: number?) -> Ray
members.name: ScreenPointToRay
members.summary: The unit ray through a screen pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals ViewportPointToRay.

members.name: VRTiltAndRollEnabled
members.summary: Whether VR tilt and roll reach the camera (default false). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

members.decl: (x: number, y: number, depth: number?) -> Ray
members.name: ViewportPointToRay
members.summary: The unit ray through a viewport pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it (default 0).

members.name: ViewportSize
members.summary: The size of the view in pixels as a Vector2 (width, height). 1×1 for a camera no eye renders through. Fires its signal on a resize.

members.name: WorldToScreenPoint
members.summary: The pixel position of a world point as (x, y, depth) — depth the distance along the look, negative behind the eye — plus whether it is on screen. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals WorldToViewportPoint.

members.name: WorldToViewportPoint
members.summary: The viewport position of a world point as (x, y, depth) in pixels from the top-left, plus whether it is inside the view and in front of the eye.

members.name: ZoomToExtents
members.summary: Backs the camera along its current look until the box's bounding sphere fits the view (radius over the sine of half the max-axis view — measured); a CFrame write like any other, so the orbit modes re-seat from it.

classes.name: Camera
classes.summary: The eye as an object: workspace.CurrentCamera is the one the process renders through (minted with the local player, none on a dedicated server); Instance.new makes further, inert cameras that CurrentCamera can be assigned. CameraType picks who drives it — the built-in orbit around CameraSubject in its several flavors, or scripts through CFrame — FieldOfView and its mode the lens, and the projection methods map between world and screen. Client-local: never saved or replicated.

members.name: AssemblyAngularVelocity
members.summary: The character body's angular velocity.

members.name: AssemblyCenterOfMass
members.summary: The character body's center of mass in world space.

members.name: AssemblyLinearVelocity
members.summary: The character body's linear velocity.

members.name: AssemblyMass
members.summary: The character body's mass.

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The character's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

members.name: CenterOfMass
members.summary: The character body's local center of mass.

members.name: Mass
members.summary: The character body's mass.

members.name: Position
members.summary: The character's world position. Writing teleports the character.

members.name: RotVelocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the character body's angular velocity — use AssemblyAngularVelocity.

members.name: Rotation
members.summary: The character's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees; writing turns the character.

members.name: Touched
members.summary: Fires when a collider starts touching the character body, with the other object.

members.name: Velocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the character body's linear velocity — use AssemblyLinearVelocity.

classes.name: Character
classes.summary: A live character body — the physical, scriptable entity a player controls, or an NPC from SpawnCharacter. One collidable part that stands in for the reference's whole rig: its pose surface and Touched are here, its brain is the Humanoid child (character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") — the body IS the part, so hit:FindFirstChildOfClass, not hit.Parent).

members.name: MaxActivationDistance
members.summary: How far away (in studs) a player can be and still click, floored at 0.

members.name: MouseClick
members.summary: Fires when a player clicks the detector's parent part within MaxActivationDistance, with the clicking player. The signal lives on the detector, never on the part it makes clickable.

classes.name: ClickDetector
classes.summary: Makes its parent part clickable: MouseClick fires with the clicking player, within MaxActivationDistance.

members.name: Attachment0
members.summary: One end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil. The constraint acts while Enabled and both ends sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert, never an error (§16). A destroyed attachment stays referenced.

members.name: Attachment1
members.summary: The other end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the constraint acts. Disabling is inert (a joint's derived joint goes away, a mover pushes nothing); re-enabling rebuilds a joint at the current poses (§16).

classes.name: Constraint
classes.summary: The base of the attachment-anchored constraints: Attachment0, Attachment1 and Enabled. A constraint acts while Enabled and the ends it needs sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert.

members.name: UseCache
members.summary: Whether GetAsync may answer from a cache: true by default (measured). The engine keeps no cache, so a read is fresh either way.

classes.name: DataStoreGetOptions
classes.summary: The options GetAsync reads: UseCache, true by default — the engine keeps no cache, so a read is fresh either way. Script-made, never saved.

members.name: GetMetadata
members.summary: The metadata SetMetadata gave — an empty table before it.

members.name: SetMetadata
members.summary: The metadata the next IncrementAsync with these options writes — a table, 300 bytes of JSON at most when the write lands.

classes.name: DataStoreIncrementOptions
classes.summary: The options IncrementAsync reads: the metadata SetMetadata gives rides the increment. Script-made, never saved.

members.name: AllScopes
members.summary: Whether GetDataStore opens the store across every scope of its name (false by default, measured) — then the scope must be "" (`DataStore scope should be an empty string allScopes is set to true`, nil meaning "global") and every key reads `<scope>/<key>`.

members.name: SetExperimentalFeatures
members.summary: Takes the reference's feature switches; { v2 = true } is accepted and kept (measured) and changes nothing here.

classes.name: DataStoreOptions
classes.summary: The options GetDataStore reads: AllScopes opens a store across every scope of its name (its keys `<scope>/<key>`), and SetExperimentalFeatures takes { v2 = true }. Script-made, never saved.

members.name: GetMetadata
members.summary: The metadata SetMetadata gave — an empty table before it.

members.name: SetMetadata
members.summary: The metadata the next SetAsync with these options writes — a table (`Unable to cast double to Dictionary` otherwise, measured), 300 bytes of JSON at most when the write lands.

classes.name: DataStoreSetOptions
classes.summary: The options SetAsync reads: the metadata SetMetadata gives rides the write and reads back through the key info. Script-made, never saved.

classes.name: Folder
classes.summary: A pure organizational container with no behavior of its own.

classes.name: FormFactorPart
classes.summary: A legacy layer between BasePart and Part, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine; it adds no members of its own.

classes.name: Frame
classes.summary: The plain rectangular UI element: a background and a parent for other elements.

classes.name: GuiBase
classes.summary: The UI root layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

classes.name: GuiBase2d
classes.summary: The 2D UI layer beneath every on-screen element.

members.name: Activated
members.summary: Fires (with no arguments) when a click is released over the button.

classes.name: GuiButton
classes.summary: The clickable UI elements: Activated fires on click release.

classes.name: GuiLabel
classes.summary: The display-only UI elements — the image and text labels.

members.name: AnchorPoint
members.summary: Which point of the element (0..1 per axis) its Position pins: (0, 0) the top-left corner, (0.5, 0.5) the center. A Vector2 — assigning anything else refuses (measured).

members.name: BackgroundColor3
members.summary: The element's fill color.

members.name: BackgroundTransparency
members.summary: How see-through the element's fill renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

members.name: LayoutOrder
members.summary: The sibling sort key a parent's UIListLayout orders by (SortOrder.LayoutOrder); lower comes first. Ignored without a layout.

members.name: Position
members.summary: The element's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis), relative to the parent element.

members.name: Size
members.summary: The element's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Whether the element renders. A hidden element hides its whole subtree and occupies no layout space.

classes.name: GuiObject
classes.summary: The visible UI elements: UDim2 Position and Size, AnchorPoint, and the background fill.

members.name: ActuatorType
members.summary: What drives the hinge: None (a free hinge, the default), Motor (turns at AngularVelocity) or Servo (turns to TargetAngle). Writes accept the Enum.ActuatorType item or its name.

members.name: AngularResponsiveness
members.summary: How stiffly the Servo pulls toward its target: 5 approaches slowly, 45 (the default) arrives without overshoot, 200 overshoots against its torque cap. Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end, an infinite one included (measured); a NaN write is refused.

members.name: AngularSpeed
members.summary: The Servo's rate cap in radians per second: its applied target moves toward TargetAngle by at most this much a second. The default 0 holds the Servo where it stands (measured).

members.name: AngularVelocity
members.summary: The Motor's target speed in radians per second: Attachment1 turns about Attachment0's X axis at it, within MotorMaxTorque and MotorMaxAcceleration. Default 0.

members.name: CurrentAngle
members.summary: The hinge's angle in degrees: Attachment1 about Attachment0's X axis, 0 with the two attachments aligned, positive turning Attachment0's Y toward its Z (measured). 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it turns.

members.name: LimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the hinge stops hard at LowerAngle and UpperAngle. Default false.

members.name: LowerAngle
members.summary: The lower limit in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default -45.

members.name: MotorMaxAcceleration
members.summary: The Motor's angular-acceleration cap in radians per second squared: its applied speed ramps toward AngularVelocity by at most this much a second (measured as a true cap). Default 500000.

members.name: MotorMaxTorque
members.summary: The most torque the Motor applies. The default 0 moves nothing (measured), as does any value of 0 or less.

members.name: Radius
members.summary: The size of the hinge's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.15.

members.name: Restitution
members.summary: The limits' bounce, clamped to 0..1 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Stored and saved, but inert: the hinge stops dead at a limit whatever it holds (a recorded divergence — the reference bounces). Default 0.

members.name: ServoMaxTorque
members.summary: The most torque the Servo applies. The default 0 moves nothing, as does any value of 0 or less.

members.name: SoftlockServoUponReachingTarget
members.summary: Deprecated on the reference. Stored and saved, inert. Default false.

members.name: TargetAngle
members.summary: The Servo's target in degrees from the two attachments aligned, reduced modulo 360 and reached the short way (270 is -90, 720 is 0 — measured). Default 0.

members.name: UpperAngle
members.summary: The upper limit in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

classes.name: HingeConstraint
classes.summary: A hinge: the two bodies rotate about the attachments' X axes — free, or driven by a Motor or a Servo (ActuatorType), within optional limits.

members.name: Died
members.summary: Fires once per life, when Health reaches zero, with the body still in the world.

members.name: DisplayName
members.summary: The name shown for the character: the body's name at spawn, empty for an Instance.new humanoid (measured). Up to 4096 bytes — the wire's limit; the reference caps nothing (recorded).

members.name: FreeFalling
members.summary: true on entering Freefall and again on Landed (the reference's own quirk, measured); false on Landed and on the return to Running.

members.name: GetMoveVelocity
members.summary: MoveDirection times WalkSpeed times the intent's length: (WalkSpeed, 0, 0) for Move(1, 0, 0), half for a half-length direction, the unit's y scaled too (measured); zero at rest.

members.name: GetState
members.summary: The current state: Running, Jumping, Freefall, Landed, Seated, PlatformStanding or Dead on a body this end simulates; None for an unparented humanoid. A replica keeps the state it was born with (only the dead latch travels).

members.name: GetStateEnabled
members.summary: Whether SetStateEnabled left the state enabled (measured: every state starts enabled).

members.name: Health
members.summary: Current health; a write clamps to 0..MaxHealth at once (measured). Reaching zero fires Died once and latches the humanoid dead — the body stays in the world until the respawn replaces it; a write on a dead humanoid reads back for the frame and is forced back to 0 on the next pass (measured) — nothing revives it. Every change fires HealthChanged, after the property's own Changed (measured order). A non-finite write is refused (the reference stores it — recorded).

members.name: HealthChanged
members.summary: Fires with the new Health on every change — and with the unchanged Health on a MaxHealth write (measured).

members.name: Jump
members.summary: A one-shot jump request: true makes the body take off on its next simulated tick (if grounded and Jumping is enabled) and reads back true until then; a seated humanoid stands up on it.

members.name: JumpPower
members.summary: The upward velocity a jump imparts, floored at 0.

members.name: Jumping
members.summary: true on takeoff, false the frame after (measured).

members.name: MaxHealth
members.summary: The ceiling the Health SETTER clamps to, floored at 0 (math.huge accepted). Lowering it leaves the current Health alone (measured: 100 over a MaxHealth of 50 stays 100) and fires HealthChanged with it.

members.name: Move
members.summary: Sets a persistent world-space walk direction: the body keeps walking until the next call, a zero vector stops it, and the length scales the speed (half a unit walks at half WalkSpeed — measured). The relativeToCamera flag is client presentation and is ignored here.

members.name: MoveDirection
members.summary: The unit direction of the last accepted Move (the controls, on a possessed body), y included; zero at rest and zero during a MoveTo; kept through sitting and death, where a Move while seated is ignored (measured).

members.name: MoveTo
members.summary: Walks the body to a point: reached within 1 stud in the horizontal plane, or given up after 8 seconds (every call restarts the timer). MoveToFinished fires with the outcome; a pending MoveTo owns locomotion over Move. With a part, the point is relative to it (WalkToPart) as it moves.

members.name: MoveToFinished
members.summary: Fires when a MoveTo ends: true when the target was reached, false on the timeout. A replaced target fires nothing.

members.name: PlatformStand
members.summary: Limp: no walking, no jumping, the PlatformStanding state (measured; skipped when SetStateEnabled turned it off); a false write returns the body to Running.

members.name: RootPart
members.summary: The body this humanoid drives — the one-part Character — or nil for a humanoid parented nowhere a body is (measured: nil fresh from Instance.new and in a Folder).

members.name: Running
members.summary: Fires with the ground speed as it changes while Running — silent in the air — and with 0 on entering any other state (measured).

members.name: SeatPart
members.summary: The seat occupied — always nil: no seat class exists yet; Sit seats in place.

members.name: Seated
members.summary: Fires (true, nil) on sitting and (false, nil) on standing up — the seat nil until a seat class exists.

members.name: SetStateEnabled
members.summary: Keeps the state machine OUT of a state, never the motion (measured): Seated or PlatformStanding off skip the state while the body still cannot walk, Jumping off refuses the player's own jump but an NPC still takes off straight into Freefall, Dead off keeps a zero-health humanoid alive and unable to walk. Takes the item or its name.

members.name: Sit
members.summary: Seated in place (no seat class exists yet, so SeatPart stays nil): the body walks nowhere and enters the Seated state with Seated(true, nil) — unless SetStateEnabled turned Seated off, when the state is skipped but the body still cannot walk (measured). A false write stands up; so does a jump on the player's own character (the reference's controls do that), while an NPC stays seated (measured).

members.name: StateChanged
members.summary: Fires (old, new) on every state transition, after the state's own signal. The capsule body walks Running, Jumping, Freefall, Landed, Seated, PlatformStanding and Dead.

members.name: TakeDamage
members.summary: Subtracts amount from Health, floored at zero — reaching zero fires Died; the body stays, dead, until the respawn replaces it. A negative amount heals, past MaxHealth too (measured).

members.name: Touched
members.summary: Fires (touchingPart, humanoidPart) when a collider starts touching the body this humanoid drives — the toucher, then the one-part body (measured shape, once per contact start, silent at rest — relayed from the body's contacts).

members.name: WalkSpeed
members.summary: The body's walk speed in studs per second, floored at 0 (measured: a negative write reads 0).

members.name: WalkToPart
members.summary: The part the last MoveTo target is relative to, or nil.

members.name: WalkToPoint
members.summary: The last MoveTo target, kept after arrival (measured). Read-only here where the reference accepts a write — a recorded divergence.

classes.name: Humanoid
classes.summary: A character's brain, a child of the body it drives: Health and MaxHealth with Died and HealthChanged, WalkSpeed and JumpPower, the one-shot Jump, Sit and PlatformStand, MoveTo/Move with MoveDirection, WalkToPoint and MoveToFinished, and the state machine — GetState, StateChanged, Running, Jumping, FreeFalling, Seated, the SetStateEnabled gates. Spawned with every body; Instance.new makes a bodiless one (RootPart nil, state None) that parenting under a body brings alive. Destroying it leaves the body standing, and it never respawns (measured).

members.name: Image
members.summary: The displayed image, as a local asset path. Unset reads as the empty string; writing the empty string clears it.

members.name: ImageColor3
members.summary: Tints the image: each texel is multiplied by this color. White (the default) draws the image as authored.

members.name: ImageTransparency
members.summary: How see-through the image itself renders (the background has its own transparency), clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

classes.name: ImageLabel
classes.summary: A UI element that displays an image asset.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the action is driven by its bindings and Fire (true by default).

members.name: Fire
members.summary: Writes the state from a script — a boolean, a number, a Vector2 or a Vector3 by the Type — firing StateChanged (and Pressed/Released for a Bool) on a real change. The way an action with no bindings is driven; bound actions are overwritten by their keys next frame.

members.name: GetState
members.summary: The current state as the Type reads it: a boolean, a number in -1..1, a Vector2 or a Vector3 — driven every frame by the InputBinding children, or by Fire when there are none.

members.name: Pressed
members.summary: Bool actions: fires with true when the state goes from released to pressed.

members.name: Released
members.summary: Bool actions: fires with false when the state goes from pressed to released.

members.name: StateChanged
members.summary: Fires with the new state whenever it changes, never for a same-state write; a held direction fires once, so poll GetState for continuous input.

members.name: Type
members.summary: What the action carries: Bool (a press), Direction1D (a number), Direction2D (a Vector2) or Direction3D (a Vector3). Writes accept the item or its name and reset the state.

classes.name: InputAction
classes.summary: One typed input under an InputContext — Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D or Direction3D — driven by its InputBinding children every frame; GetState reads it, StateChanged/Pressed/Released fire on change.

members.name: Backward
members.summary: The composite key for +Z; None when unset.

members.name: ClampMagnitudeToOne
members.summary: Whether a composite direction longer than 1 (two keys at once) is clamped to unit length before the scales (true by default).

members.name: Down
members.summary: The composite key for -Y; None when unset.

members.name: Forward
members.summary: The composite key for -Z (a Direction3D's (0, 0, -1)); None when unset.

members.name: KeyCode
members.summary: The key driving a Bool action (pressed) or a Direction1D one (+1); None when unset. Writes accept the item, its name, or None (Unknown, its legacy name, too) to clear.

members.name: Left
members.summary: The composite key for -X (a Direction2D's (-1, 0)); None when unset.

members.name: PrimaryModifier
members.summary: A key that must be held for the binding to count; None (the default) requires none.

members.name: Right
members.summary: The composite key for +X; None when unset.

members.name: Scale
members.summary: A multiplier on every component of a directional action's output (1 by default), applied after the clamp.

members.name: SecondaryModifier
members.summary: A second key that must be held for the binding to count; None (the default) requires none.

members.name: Up
members.summary: The composite key for +Y (a Direction1D's +1, a Direction2D's (0, 1), a Direction3D's (0, 1, 0)); None when unset.

members.name: Vector2Scale
members.summary: A per-component multiplier on a Direction2D action's output ((1, 1) by default), applied after the clamp.

members.name: Vector3Scale
members.summary: A per-component multiplier on a Direction3D action's output ((1, 1, 1) by default), applied after the clamp.

classes.name: InputBinding
classes.summary: One key binding under an InputAction: KeyCode for a Bool or Direction1D action, the Up/Down/Left/Right/Forward/Backward keys for a directional one, modifiers that must be held, the output scales and the unit-length clamp.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the context's actions are read at all (true by default). A disabled context's actions hold their last state.

members.name: Priority
members.summary: Contexts are read in descending priority (0 by default; an integer, a fraction truncates): a higher context's Sink consumes keys before a lower one sees them.

members.name: Sink
members.summary: When true, the keys this context's bindings read are consumed at its priority and never reach lower-priority contexts (false by default).

classes.name: InputContext
classes.summary: A group of InputActions: contexts are read in descending Priority, and a Sink context consumes the keys its bindings use before lower-priority contexts see them. Under a Player, its actions' states reach the server.

members.name: AncestryChanged
members.summary: Fires when this instance or any ancestor is reparented, on every node of the moved subtree (deepest first), with the MOVED instance and its new parent — nil on detach. Destroy fires each destroyed node's own (self, nil).

members.name: Archivable
members.summary: Whether Clone copies the instance: true by default. A non-archivable instance's Clone returns nil, and a clone of its parent leaves it and its subtree out; a character is born non-archivable. A runtime flag: neither saved nor replicated, never copied by Clone, and a boolean only.

members.name: AttributeChanged
members.summary: Fires with the attribute NAME on every landed attribute write — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Delivers once per landed write in write order, before the matching GetAttributeChangedSignal.

members.name: Changed
members.summary: Fires with the property NAME on every landed property write — pose writes fan out to CFrame, Position and Rotation; same-value writes stay silent; attribute writes travel their own AttributeChanged channel; physics motion never fires. The value containers override it entirely: their Changed fires only for Value, with the new VALUE as payload.

members.name: ChildAdded
members.summary: Fires when an instance is parented directly under this one. The listener receives the added child.

members.name: ChildRemoved
members.summary: Fires when a direct child is unparented from this instance or destroyed. The listener receives the removed child.

members.name: ClassName
members.summary: The instance's class, as a string. An instance never changes class. Prefer IsA over comparing ClassName — IsA also matches base classes like BasePart.

members.name: ClearAllChildren
members.summary: Destroys every direct child and its subtree — the last child first, each node's Destroying before its children's — and leaves the instance itself in place. The cleared nodes are husks: parentless and locked. On a destroyed instance it does nothing.

members.name: Clone
members.summary: A deep copy of the instance and its subtree: authored state, attributes and tags copy; the copy is detached (Parent is nil) with fresh identity. A destroyed instance clones its husk as a live single-node copy.

members.name: DescendantAdded
members.summary: Fires when an instance is added anywhere in this instance's subtree, with the added descendant. When a whole subtree is attached it fires for the attached node itself, not for every instance below it.

members.name: Destroy
members.summary: Destroys the instance and its whole subtree, firing Destroying. Destroyed instances stay readable as husks: properties read their last values, Parent reads nil and is locked. Destroying an already-destroyed instance does nothing.

members.name: Destroying
members.summary: Fires when the instance is destroyed. The listener sees a husk: properties still read their last values, the tree is severed, and Parent reads nil.

members.name: FindFirstAncestor
members.summary: The nearest ancestor named name, or nil. The chain ends at the DataModel: game's Name matches last (measured).

members.name: FindFirstAncestorOfClass
members.summary: The nearest ancestor whose ClassName is exactly className, or nil. FindFirstAncestorOfClass("DataModel") answers game from any rooted instance (measured).

members.name: FindFirstAncestorWhichIsA
members.summary: The nearest ancestor that IsA(className), or nil — game answers for DataModel, ServiceProvider and (with no nearer match) Instance, its measured ancestry.

members.name: FindFirstChild
members.summary: The first direct child named name, or nil. The cheap probe when absence is an expected answer — cache the result instead of re-finding it every frame.

members.name: FindFirstChildOfClass
members.summary: The first direct child whose ClassName is exactly className, or nil. Never recursive (measured: a second argument is ignored) — FindFirstChildWhichIsA is the one that descends.

members.name: FindFirstChildWhichIsA
members.summary: The first direct child that IsA(className), or nil; with recursive true the whole subtree is searched in GetDescendants order.

members.name: GetAttribute
members.summary: The named attribute — a bare value for primitives, a table of fields for records — or nil when unset. The two-argument form is a BetterVoxel extension: it projects one field of a record as a bare value without building the table — the cheap shape for hot loops (nil on primitives).

members.name: GetAttributeChangedSignal
members.summary: A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named attribute lands a change on this instance — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Any attribute name is legal, set or not. Delivers after the instance-wide AttributeChanged for the same write.

members.name: GetAttributes
members.summary: Every attribute of the instance as a fresh table of name to value — a bare value for primitives, a table of fields for records — empty when none is set. The table is a copy: writing it changes no attribute (SetAttribute does).

members.name: GetChildren
members.summary: The direct children, in child order, as an array. A destroyed instance answers an empty array.

members.name: GetDescendants
members.summary: Every instance below this one as an array, in preorder: each node comes before its own children.

members.name: GetFullName
members.summary: The instance's full dot-joined path from the root, Workspace included: 'Workspace.Folder.Part'. A detached instance's full name is just its Name — member errors quote this same spelling.

members.name: GetPropertyChangedSignal
members.summary: A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named property changes on this instance. Explicit writes fire it; physics motion never fires the pose properties. Subscribing errors when the property can never fire on this class — the same catch-the-typo philosophy as unknown member names.

members.name: IsA
members.summary: Whether the instance's class is className or inherits from it: a Part IsA 'BasePart' and IsA 'Instance'. Unknown class names answer false.

members.name: IsAncestorOf
members.summary: Whether this instance sits anywhere above descendant (self does not count; nil answers false — measured, asymmetric with IsDescendantOf).

members.name: IsDescendantOf
members.summary: Whether ancestor sits anywhere above this instance (self does not count). game counts for every rooted instance, and nil answers TRUE — the measured quirk: every chain ends at nil.

members.name: Name
members.summary: The instance's name — the label the Explorer shows and the key FindFirstChild, WaitForChild and dot-child access match on. Names need not be unique among siblings; lookups return the first match in child order.

members.name: Parent
members.summary: The instance's parent in the object tree, or nil for a detached root; a Player's is the Players service while it is in the game (measured). Assigning Parent reparents without moving anything in world space; assigning nil detaches the subtree without destroying it. Locked after Destroy.

members.name: PredictionMode
members.summary: Whether a client predicts this instance under server authority (net-sync-v2 §2.9): Automatic unless RunService:SetPredictionMode forced it On or Off on this client. Read-only; the reference shows it in Studio only under server authority.

members.name: Remove
members.summary: Deprecated: sets the Parent of this instance and of every descendant to nil, top-down, each node leaving with the ordinary signals of a reparent. Nothing is destroyed or locked: every node can take a parent again. On a destroyed instance it does nothing. Use Destroy to destroy, or set Parent to nil to detach.

members.decl: (name: string, value: boolean | number | string | Vector3 | Color3 | CFrame | {[string]: any} | nil) -> ()
members.name: SetAttribute

params.name: value
params.type: boolean | number | string | Vector3 | Color3 | CFrame | {[string]: any} | nil

members.summary: Writes the named attribute: a primitive or datatype (Vector3, Color3, CFrame) stores directly, a table stores a structured record, and nil REMOVES the attribute (also the way to change its type: remove, then set). Writes coerce onto the attribute's declared shape — out-of-range values error, a record write merges field by field with missing fields keeping their values. Every landed write fires AttributeChanged then the per-name signal; same-value writes are silent. Names are capped at 100 characters and cannot be empty; non-finite components refuse.

members.name: WaitForChild
members.summary: The first direct child named name, suspending the calling thread until one exists. A child already present returns without yielding. With a timeout (in seconds) the wait gives up and returns nil once it elapses; without one it waits forever.

members.name: changed
members.summary: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Changed, answered the same way — a value container's is its value signal — use Changed.

members.name: clone
members.summary: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Clone, answered the same way — use Clone.

members.name: destroy
members.summary: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Destroy, answered the same way — use Destroy.

members.name: findFirstChild
members.summary: Deprecated: the retired spelling of FindFirstChild, answered the same way — use FindFirstChild.

members.name: new
members.summary: A default-constructed instance of the named class, with Parent nil — assign Parent to bring it into the world (derived state appears on attach). Only creatable classes are accepted; abstract and engine-spawned classes error exactly like an unknown name.

members.name: remove
members.summary: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Remove, answered the same way.

classes.name: Instance
classes.summary: The root of the class tree: identity (Name, ClassName), the Parent tree with its hierarchy signals, attributes, and lifetime (Clone, Destroy). Every scriptable object is an Instance.

members.name: Value
members.summary: The stored integer. Number writes round half away from zero (3.5 becomes 4, -3.7 becomes -4).

classes.name: IntValue
classes.summary: A named container for one integer; number writes round half away from zero.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the joint acts: Enabled, parented in the tree, both ends set to two different parts in the tree, and not both of them anchored (two anchored parts each root an assembly of their own; measured, §43).

members.name: C0
members.summary: The joint's frame in Part0's space: while Active, Part0.CFrame * C0 equals Part1.CFrame * C1. Writing it moves the part that is not the assembly root on the next physics pass (measured, §43).

members.name: C1
members.summary: The joint's frame in Part1's space — C0's counterpart.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the joint may act (Active also needs both ends). Disabling leaves the parts where they stand; re-enabling stands the non-root part where C0 and C1 put it (measured, §43).

members.name: Part0
members.summary: The part C0 is a frame of: an Instance or nil. Setting an end of an active joint moves the part that is not the assembly root to where the frames put it (§43).

members.name: Part1
members.summary: The part C1 is a frame of: an Instance or nil.

classes.name: JointInstance
classes.summary: The base of the classic joints: Part0 and Part1, the frames C0 and C1 they are held at, Enabled, and the read-only Active.

classes.name: LayerCollector
classes.summary: The UI roots that collect an element tree: ScreenGui on the screen, BillboardGui in the world.

members.name: Brightness
members.summary: The light's intensity, floored at 0. The unit is the renderer's (a default light reads 1000000), not the reference engine's 0..~10 scale — a recorded divergence.

members.name: Color
members.summary: The light's color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the light is lit. Disabling removes the derived render light; the authored properties keep their values.

members.name: Range
members.summary: How far the light reaches, in studs, floored at 0.

members.name: Shadows
members.summary: Whether the light casts shadows.

classes.name: Light
classes.summary: The shared light surface: Brightness, Color, Range, Shadows and the Enabled switch, parented under the part that carries the light.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the velocity target acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it; a zero MaxForce leaves it active (measured). Read only.

members.name: ForceLimitMode
members.summary: Magnitude (the default) holds the force's length to MaxForce; PerAxis holds each axis of RelativeTo's frame to its lane of MaxAxesForce in Vector mode, each tangent axis to its lane of MaxPlanarAxesForce in Plane mode (a line keeps MaxForce).

members.name: ForceLimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the force is limited (by ForceLimitMode); off, the target is reached within the step whatever it takes. Default true.

members.name: LineDirection
members.summary: The line Line mode holds the velocity along, in RelativeTo's frame (its length ignored; the zero vector holds nothing). Default (1, 0, 0).

members.name: LineVelocity
members.summary: The speed held along LineDirection in Line mode, studs per second. Default 0.

members.name: MaxAxesForce
members.summary: The most force along each axis of RelativeTo's frame under the PerAxis limit in Vector mode; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (1000, 1000, 1000).

members.name: MaxForce
members.summary: The most force, the assembly's weight included, under the Magnitude limit (and along a line under either), while ForceLimitsEnabled: the acceleration is MaxForce / mass until the target is reached (measured). Default 1000.

members.name: MaxPlanarAxesForce
members.summary: The most force along each tangent axis under the PerAxis limit in Plane mode; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (1000, 1000).

members.name: PlaneVelocity
members.summary: The velocity held along the two tangent axes in Plane mode, studs per second. Default (0, 0).

members.name: PrimaryTangentAxis
members.summary: Plane mode's first axis, in RelativeTo's frame. Default (1, 0, 0).

members.name: ReactionForceEnabled
members.summary: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite force under RelativeTo Attachment1, the pair then sharing its momentum (an equal pair, one moving 3, ends at 1.5 each — measured). Default true.

members.name: RelativeTo
members.summary: The frame the target velocity, the line, the plane and the per-axis limits are named in: the world's (the default), Attachment0's, or Attachment1's — the velocity then relative to Attachment1's assembly.

members.name: SecondaryTangentAxis
members.summary: Plane mode's second axis, in RelativeTo's frame, made perpendicular to the first. Default (0, 1, 0).

members.name: VectorVelocity
members.summary: The velocity held in Vector mode, studs per second, in RelativeTo's frame: reached within a step while the force limit allows (measured). Default (0, 0, 0).

members.name: VelocityConstraintMode
members.summary: What the target holds: Vector (the default) the whole velocity, Line its component along LineDirection, Plane its projection on the two tangent axes.

members.name: Visible
members.summary: Draws the editor's marker for the velocity target whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

classes.name: LinearVelocity
classes.summary: A mover: a force that brings Attachment0's assembly to a velocity within each physics step — the whole vector, its component along a line, or its projection on a plane, named in RelativeTo's frame — within its force limits, the assembly's weight held.

classes.name: LocalScript
classes.summary: A script that runs on each client. Its CLASS decides that — a stored RunContext value is accepted but inert.

classes.name: LuaSourceContainer
classes.summary: Anything that holds Luau source: the scripts and modules.

members.name: MeshId
members.summary: The mesh asset reference, as the asset's local path — the empty string on a meshless husk. Every write is refused: the mesh reference is immutable after authoring.

members.name: MeshSize
members.summary: The authored mesh bounds, untouched by resizes. Every write is refused; resize through Size, which scales the mesh against these bounds.

classes.name: MeshPart
classes.summary: A part whose geometry is an imported mesh. Size scales the mesh against its authored MeshSize; collision comes from the baked CollisionFidelity shapes; the mesh reference itself is immutable.

members.name: GetBoundingBox
members.summary: The axis-aligned box around the subtree's parts, as (center CFrame, size). Errors when the subtree holds no part.

members.name: GetPrimaryPartCFrame
members.summary: Deprecated: the PrimaryPart's CFrame. Errors when the model has no PrimaryPart or it no longer exists. Use GetPivot.

members.name: PrimaryPart
members.summary: The part the model pivots through, or nil. GetPivot and PivotTo use it; without one they fall back to the bounding-box center. A reference to a despawned part reads as nil.

members.name: SetPrimaryPartCFrame
members.summary: Deprecated: moves the model by one rigid transform so its PrimaryPart lands at cframe — PivotTo through the PrimaryPart. Errors when the model has no PrimaryPart or it no longer exists. Use PivotTo.

classes.name: Model
classes.summary: A grouping node for parts: pivots through PrimaryPart (or its bounding-box center without one) and moves as a group via PivotTo.

classes.name: ModuleScript
classes.summary: Reusable code loaded with require: runs once per context, and its return value is cached and shared between requirers.

members.name: Value
members.summary: The stored double-precision number.

classes.name: NumberValue
classes.summary: A named container for one double-precision number.

members.name: Value
members.summary: The stored instance reference, or nil. References outlive Destroy — a destroyed target reads as its husk; assigning nil clears the slot.

classes.name: ObjectValue
classes.summary: A named container for one instance reference; references survive Destroy and read back as husks.

members.name: GetPivot
members.summary: The instance's pivot: a Model's PrimaryPart pose (or its bounding-box center without one), an ordinary part's own CFrame.

members.name: PivotTo
members.summary: Moves this instance and its logical descendants by ONE rigid transform: the subtree lands with its pivot at the target CFrame, members orbiting the pivot and rotating with it. A plain vector keeps the current rotation. Fires the pose signals for each moved object. A PrimaryPart-less Model pivots about its bounding-box center with identity rotation, so repeated ROTATING pivots compound there — a recorded divergence; give the model a PrimaryPart.

classes.name: PVInstance
classes.summary: The positioned layer: everything with a pivot — parts and models — answers GetPivot and moves as a group through PivotTo.

members.name: Shape
members.summary: The part's geometric shape. Writes accept the Enum.PartType item or its string name; the mesh and collider re-derive.

classes.name: Part
classes.summary: The basic building block: a shaped, colored, physically simulated solid. Shape picks the geometry; the mesh and collider re-derive.

members.name: Acceleration
members.summary: A constant acceleration applied to every particle, in studs per second squared (gravity is not applied on its own).

members.name: Brightness
members.summary: A multiplier on the particle color (1 is unchanged; stored as written).

members.name: Clear
members.summary: Removes every live particle of this emitter now.

members.name: Color
members.summary: The particle color over its lifetime, as a ColorSequence (a Color3 is refused — wrap it in ColorSequence.new).

members.name: Drag
members.summary: Velocity damping per second (0 is none); stored as written.

members.name: EmissionDirection
members.summary: The face of the parent part particles leave from. Writes accept the Enum.NormalId item or its name.

members.name: Emit
members.summary: Spawns particleCount particles at once (default 16), Enabled or not — local to the calling context, never replicated. A negative count is a no-op; a string refuses.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the emitter spawns at its Rate. Live particles finish their lives either way; Emit works while disabled.

members.name: FastForward
members.summary: Advances the emitter as if seconds had already passed — the steady state without the warm-up. Public here (an engine extension); zero or negative is a no-op.

members.name: FlipbookFramerate
members.summary: Frames per second of the flipbook, picked uniformly within the range per particle.

members.name: FlipbookLayout
members.summary: The sprite grid the Texture holds: None, Grid2x2, Grid4x4 or Grid8x8 (Custom is refused — the engine has no custom grids).

members.name: FlipbookMode
members.summary: How the grid plays over a particle's life: Loop, OneShot, PingPong or Random.

members.name: FlipbookStartRandom
members.summary: Whether each particle starts the flipbook on a random frame.

members.name: Lifetime
members.summary: Each particle's life in seconds, picked uniformly within the range.

members.name: LightEmission
members.summary: The blend from normal (0) to additive (1) — glowing particles lighten what is behind them; stored as written.

members.name: LightInfluence
members.summary: How much the scene's lighting affects the particles (0 unlit, 1 lit like a surface); stored as written.

members.name: LockedToPart
members.summary: Whether particles move with the parent after spawning (local space) instead of staying where they were born (world space).

members.name: Orientation
members.summary: How the particle quad faces: the camera, the camera about the world up, or along/across its velocity (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).

members.name: Rate
members.summary: Particles spawned per second while Enabled. Stored as written (the reference accepts any number); a negative rate spawns nothing.

members.name: RotSpeed
members.summary: The spin in degrees per second, picked uniformly within the range.

members.name: Rotation
members.summary: The initial spin angle in degrees, picked uniformly within the range (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).

members.name: Shape
members.summary: The emission volume: Box, Sphere, Cylinder or Disc. Writes accept the Enum.ParticleEmitterShape item or its name.

members.name: ShapeInOut
members.summary: Which way particles leave the Shape: Outward, Inward or both.

members.name: ShapePartial
members.summary: How much of the Shape emits (1 is all of it); stored as written.

members.name: ShapeStyle
members.summary: Whether particles spawn throughout the Shape (Volume) or on its boundary (Surface).

members.name: Size
members.summary: The particle size in studs over its lifetime, as a NumberSequence (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).

members.name: Speed
members.summary: The initial speed in studs per second, picked uniformly within the range.

members.name: SpreadAngle
members.summary: The emission cone half-angles in degrees, per axis, around the EmissionDirection.

members.name: Squash
members.summary: The particle's stretch over its lifetime: positive squashes along the velocity, negative stretches (0 is round).

members.name: Texture
members.summary: The particle image, as a local asset path; the empty string is the engine's built-in soft disc. Strictly a string.

members.name: TimeScale
members.summary: A multiplier on this emitter's clock (1 is real time), floored at 0 — the one particle property the reference clamps.

members.name: Transparency
members.summary: The particle transparency over its lifetime, as a NumberSequence (0 opaque, 1 invisible).

members.name: VelocityInheritance
members.summary: How much of the parent's velocity a new particle inherits (0 none, 1 all).

members.name: ZOffset
members.summary: A render offset toward the camera in studs (positive is closer) — the ordering knob, since particles are not depth-sorted.

classes.name: ParticleEmitter
classes.summary: A particle emitter under a part or an attachment: the flat property set (Rate, Lifetime, Speed, the Size/Transparency/Color sequences, the shape and flipbook enums, …) describes the effect, and each client's particle system realizes it — a headless server holds the description only. Emit, Clear and FastForward are local to the calling context. Enabled, Brightness, Color, Transparency, Shape, Size, Rotation and Orientation are the names it shares with other classes, each with its own particle-typed meaning here (docs/particle-system.md).

members.name: Character
members.summary: The player's current character body — a dead one included, until the respawn replaces it — or nil while none is loaded (before the first spawn, with CharacterAutoLoads off, or once the player is leaving). CharacterAdded fires with each new one, CharacterRemoving with each one leaving.

members.name: CharacterAdded
members.summary: Fires with the new character on every spawn, the first included.

members.name: CharacterRemoving
members.summary: Fires with the character just taken out of the world — the dead body a respawn replaces, the one LoadCharacter replaces, or a leaving player's. Delivered after the swap (measured): the old body's Parent is already nil and Character already the next body (nil on a leave), the old instance still readable; CharacterAdded follows in the same frame. The engine destroys the old body a frame later.

members.name: DisplayName
members.summary: The player's Name (measured: Studio's test players and the signed-in account alike, a player that has left too). A script's write is refused with the reference's text, on the server and the client alike (measured): `The current thread cannot set 'Player's display name' (lacking capability WritePlayer)`.

members.name: GetCameraState
members.summary: The player's camera state under server authority: CFrame, FieldOfView and ViewportSize. The CFrame rides the player's input stream, synchronized with the inputs of the same simulation tick (the server reads the camera the player's tick was played under — aim and look-direction logic); the other two replicate as properties do, at their own cadence. The server answers it for any player, a client only for its LocalPlayer; raises under the classic networking model.

members.name: GetMouse
members.summary: The player's mouse — the legacy cursor object (X/Y, UnitRay, Hit, Target, TargetFilter, Icon, the button and Move signals) built from the current camera and the local cursor. One object per player, the same on every call; a player that is not this process's reads the defaults and hears no signal.

members.name: GetNetworkPing
members.summary: One-way network latency to this player's machine in seconds (half the measured round trip). The server answers it for any connected player; a client only for its LocalPlayer — a remote player reads -1 (measured: the reference's no-measurement sentinel), and any player in solo play reads 0 (no transport). Sampled, not instantaneous: it averages the transport's last five probes (one every ~5 s) off frame-boundary clock reads, so it floors near a frame's latency on a local link and trails a link that has just degraded.

members.name: Kick
members.summary: Removes the player from the game with an optional message (a number is taken as its text). The server may kick any player: its client's console prints `Server Kick Message: <message>; Metadata: `, its session ends and its world stays as it stood, and PlayerRemoving fires wherever the player is still held. A client may kick its LocalPlayer alone — another raises 'Cannot kick a non-local Player from a LocalScript' — which ends its session. In solo play the player leaves and no other joins for the rest of the run.

members.name: LoadCharacter
members.summary: Deprecated: the former name of LoadCharacterAsync, answered the same way — use LoadCharacterAsync.

members.name: LoadCharacterAsync
members.summary: Replaces the player's current character (dead or alive) with a fresh one, suspending the calling thread until the swap has landed: CharacterRemoving fires with the old one, CharacterAdded with the new one, and Character is the new one on return. The manual route when CharacterAutoLoads is off; the server's alone. Never returns in a place without a PlayerPrefab to load from.

members.name: PlayerGui
members.summary: The player's per-player UI container, engine-spawned at join and despawned with the player. Resolved by class, so renaming it does not hide it. Contents are client-local in v1 — UI neither serializes nor replicates.

members.name: RespawnTime
members.summary: Seconds between this player's death and their respawn, floored at 0. An engine extension over the Players service's RespawnTime: joins seed it from the service value, and a per-player write wins until the next service-level write (which writes through to the whole roster).

members.name: UserId
members.summary: Who the player is beyond its connection — what a save is keyed by, as far as the server can tell. A joined player reads what the server's identity policy settles on: its join number (1, 2, 3 … per server process), a guest's negative id of that session alone, the id its client claims, or a fold of its name — one player holds an id at a time. Solo play's player is -1, Studio's own id for its first test player (measured). Below 2^53 in magnitude, so it survives Luau's number type.

classes.name: Player
classes.summary: A joined player's roster identity: UserId, the current Character (a dead one included until its respawn) with the CharacterAdded and CharacterRemoving signals, LoadCharacter, and the per-player RespawnTime (an engine extension — the reference engine keeps it on the Players service). Engine-spawned only; scripts reach players through the Players service.

classes.name: PlayerGui
classes.summary: A player's UI container, engine-spawned under each Player at join. ScreenGuis parented here render for the LOCAL player only; contents are client-local (never saved, never replicated in v1).

members.name: AssemblyAngularVelocity
members.summary: The prefab body's angular velocity (zero without a live body).

members.name: AssemblyCenterOfMass
members.summary: The prefab body's center of mass in world space.

members.name: AssemblyLinearVelocity
members.summary: The prefab body's linear velocity (zero without a live body).

members.name: AssemblyMass
members.summary: The prefab body's mass (zero without a live body).

members.name: CFrame
members.summary: The prefab's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

members.name: CenterOfMass
members.summary: The prefab body's local center of mass.

members.name: Mass
members.summary: The prefab body's mass (zero without a live body).

members.name: Position
members.summary: The prefab's world position — where characters spawned from it stand.

members.name: RotVelocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the prefab body's angular velocity — use AssemblyAngularVelocity.

members.name: Rotation
members.summary: The prefab's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees.

members.name: SpawnCharacter
