members.summary: Spawns an unowned (NPC) character from this template and returns it, placed at position or standing on the prefab's own pose. Its Humanoid child answers the humanoid surface (Health, MoveTo, ...).

members.name: Touched
members.summary: Fires when a collider starts touching the prefab body, with the other object.

members.name: Velocity
members.summary: Deprecated: the prefab body's linear velocity — use AssemblyLinearVelocity.

classes.name: PlayerPrefab
classes.summary: The character template: joining players spawn their characters from it, SpawnCharacter builds NPCs from it, and its pose is where they stand.

classes.name: PointLight
classes.summary: A light radiating in every direction from its parent's position.

members.name: FireAllClients
members.summary: Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on every connected client with these arguments.

members.name: FireClient
members.summary: Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on the given player's client with these arguments.

members.name: FireServer
members.summary: Client-side only: queues OnServerEvent on the server with these arguments. Payloads cross the remote codec — a real deep copy, even solo.

members.name: OnClientEvent
members.summary: Fires on a client when the server calls FireClient or FireAllClients, with the fired arguments. Client-side only.

members.name: OnServerEvent
members.summary: Fires on the server when a client calls FireServer: the listener receives the sending player, then the fired arguments. Server-side only — touching it on a client errors.

classes.name: RemoteEvent
classes.summary: The cross-network signal: FireServer and FireClient/FireAllClients queue OnServerEvent and OnClientEvent on the far side, payloads deep-copied through the remote codec.

members.name: InvokeClient
members.summary: Server-side only: calls the given player's OnClientInvoke and suspends until the reply, the player's disconnect (fails fast), or the timeout.

members.name: InvokeServer
members.summary: Client-side only: calls the server's OnServerInvoke and suspends the calling thread until the reply arrives — or an engine timeout errors it (the reference engine blocks forever; a recorded divergence). A handler error re-raises here with its text intact.

members.name: OnClientInvoke
members.summary: The client-side handler InvokeClient calls: it receives the arguments and its returns cross back to the server. Assign a function or nil; client-side only.

members.name: OnServerInvoke
members.summary: The server-side handler InvokeServer calls: it receives the invoking player, then the arguments, and its returns cross back to the caller. Assign a function or nil; server-side only.

classes.name: RemoteFunction
classes.summary: The cross-network call: InvokeServer and InvokeClient suspend the calling thread until the far handler's reply crosses back.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the rod acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored. Read only.

members.name: CurrentDistance
members.summary: The distance between the attachments in studs, read off the bodies; 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it moves.

members.name: Length
members.summary: The separation the rod holds its attachments at, in studs, rigidly. The measured default is 5; negative writes clamp to 0, as the rope's.

members.name: LimitAngle0
members.summary: The cone's half angle at Attachment0 in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Stored and saved, but inert: the rod turns freely at both ends (a recorded divergence). Default 90.

members.name: LimitAngle1
members.summary: The cone's half angle at Attachment1 in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Stored and saved, but inert, as LimitAngle0. Default 90.

members.name: LimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the rod's angle at each attachment is held within LimitAngle0 and LimitAngle1. Stored and saved, but inert: the rod turns freely at both ends (a recorded divergence). Default false.

members.name: Thickness
members.summary: The thickness of the rod's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.1.

classes.name: RodConstraint
classes.summary: A rigid rod: the two attachments held Length apart, both free to turn.

members.name: Length
members.summary: The rope's maximum separation in studs — slack allowed, it never pushes. The measured default is 5; negative writes clamp to 0.

classes.name: RopeConstraint
classes.summary: A slack-allowed distance cap: the bodies never separate beyond Length, and the rope never pushes.

members.name: DisplayOrder
members.summary: Stacking among ScreenGuis: higher draws on top; equal orders stack by creation.

members.name: Enabled
members.summary: Whether the ScreenGui's whole tree renders and receives input (true by default). Elements keep their state while disabled.

members.name: IgnoreGuiInset
members.summary: Extends the tree under the reference engine's top inset. A recorded no-op here: the engine draws no inset, so the value stores and changes nothing.

classes.name: ScreenGui
classes.summary: The screen-space UI root: its element tree renders over the viewport while Enabled.

classes.name: Script
classes.summary: A server-side script by default; RunContext can re-home it. Enabled is its run switch — disabling kills its threads, re-enabling restarts it fresh.

members.name: DidLoop
members.summary: Fires per looped wrap with the SoundId and the loop count since Play — the engine clock's estimate, once the clip duration is known from the audio container's header.

members.name: Ended
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId when a non-looped sound reaches its natural end (never on Stop). Playback ends where audio plays: on a dedicated server this signal never fires.

members.name: IsPaused
members.summary: The measured pause latch: set by Pause (even on a stopped sound), cleared by Play and Resume, untouched by Stop.

members.name: IsPlaying
members.summary: Whether the sound is audibly playing — Play/Stop/Pause/Resume drive it, a finished non-looped sound writes it back to false, and a paused sound reads false.

members.name: Loaded
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId when the audio asset finishes loading. Assets load where audio plays: on a dedicated server this signal never fires.

members.name: LoopRegion
members.summary: The span a looped sound loops inside while PlaybackRegionsEnabled — play through once, then wrap from its max back to its min (the intro-then-loop music shape).

members.name: Looped
members.summary: Whether playback restarts from the top when the clip ends.

members.name: Pause
members.summary: Freezes playback in place: IsPlaying reads false, TimePosition holds, and the latch shows in IsPaused. Play restarts from the top; Resume continues from here. The measured contract.

members.name: Paused
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId when the pause latch engages.

members.name: Play
members.summary: Starts playback (IsPlaying becomes true) — from a still-pending explicit TimePosition write (the authored value included), otherwise from 0. Calling Play on a playing sound restarts it from the top. The measured reference contract.

members.name: PlaybackRegion
members.summary: The playable span in seconds while PlaybackRegionsEnabled: playback starts at its min and a one-shot ends at its max (the measured fresh range is 0..60000).

members.name: PlaybackRegionsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the playback regions apply: playback then starts at PlaybackRegion's min, a one-shot ends at its max, and a looped sound loops inside LoopRegion.

members.name: PlaybackSpeed
members.summary: Playback rate (1 is normal speed), clamped to 0..20 — the measured reference range. Pitch follows the rate.

members.name: Played
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId on every acted Play — restarts included, and remotely applied plays too.

members.name: Resume
members.summary: Plays from the CURRENT TimePosition with no rewind — a paused sound continues, and (measured) even a stopped sound starts where it stands.

members.name: Resumed
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId when the latch releases into playback (Resume; a fresh Play fires Played instead).

members.name: RollOffMaxDistance
members.summary: Positional playback is silent at and beyond this distance in studs (floored at 0), whatever the roll-off mode.

members.name: RollOffMinDistance
members.summary: Positional playback holds full volume within this distance in studs (floored at 0); attenuation starts beyond it.

members.name: RollOffMode
members.summary: The attenuation curve between RollOffMinDistance and RollOffMaxDistance: Inverse (the default), Linear, LinearSquare, or InverseTapered. Writes accept the Enum.RollOffMode item or its string name.

members.name: SoundGroup
members.summary: The volume bus this sound plays through: a SoundGroup instance or nil. Assigning anything else errors.

members.name: SoundId
members.summary: The audio asset, as a local asset path.

members.name: Stop
members.summary: Stops a playing sound and rewinds TimePosition to 0 (IsPlaying becomes false). On a sound that is not playing it is a no-op — a pending TimePosition write survives. The measured contract.

members.name: Stopped
members.summary: Fires with the SoundId when Stop acts (a no-op Stop is silent; the natural end fires Ended instead).

members.name: TimeLength
members.summary: The clip length in seconds, 0 until the engine knows it — resolved from the audio container's header under the host's asset root (the reference also reads 0 before load).

members.name: TimePosition
members.summary: Playback position in seconds, stored as written (playback treats a negative as 0). Advances while the sound plays (an engine-side estimate); writing it seeks a playing sound, and a written position still pending when Play is called is where playback starts (measured).

members.name: Volume
members.summary: Playback volume, clamped to 0..10 (the measured reference range). The effective loudness multiplies in the assigned SoundGroup's Volume.

classes.name: Sound
classes.summary: A playable audio source: Play and Stop drive it, IsPlaying reads back, and volume, speed and looping are properties.

members.name: Volume
members.summary: The bus multiplier, clamped to 0..10 like Sound.Volume: every Sound in the group plays at its own Volume times this.

classes.name: SoundGroup
classes.summary: A volume bus: every Sound whose SoundGroup points here plays at its own Volume multiplied by the group's.

classes.name: SpawnLocation
classes.summary: A Part players spawn on. Otherwise a regular part — every BasePart member applies.

members.name: Angle
members.summary: The full cone angle in degrees, clamped 0..180 (writing 200 reads back 180). A default spot light reads 90.

classes.name: SpotLight
classes.summary: A cone light aimed along its parent's orientation; Angle is the full cone in degrees.

members.name: Active
members.summary: Whether the spring acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored (an anchored end leaves it active, as a hinge's anchored axle — measured). Read only.

members.name: Coils
members.summary: The number of coils the spring's marker draws: cosmetic. Default 3.

members.name: CurrentLength
members.summary: The distance between the attachments in studs, read off the bodies; 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it moves.

members.name: Damping
members.summary: How quickly the spring's oscillation dies down: a force of Damping per stud a second of the attachments' relative speed. 0 (the default) oscillates on; on the measured hung cube 60 settles and 5 still swings after 6 seconds.

members.name: FreeLength
members.summary: The length the spring rests at, in studs: further apart it pulls, closer it pushes. Default 1.

members.name: LimitsEnabled
members.summary: Whether the spring's length stops hard at MinLength and MaxLength, without a bounce. Default false.

members.name: MaxForce
members.summary: The most force the spring applies. Stored and saved, but inert: the spring's force is never capped (a recorded divergence). Default inf.

members.name: MaxLength
members.summary: The most separation the spring allows while LimitsEnabled, in studs. Default 5.

members.name: MinLength
members.summary: The least separation the spring allows while LimitsEnabled, in studs. Default 0.

members.name: Radius
members.summary: The radius of the spring marker's coils in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.4.

members.name: Stiffness
members.summary: The spring's force per stud of stretch past FreeLength (or of compression short of it): a 5.6-mass cube hung on Stiffness 100 rests about 11 studs past FreeLength, k·x = m·g (the reference 10.979, the engine 10.960 where the cube falls asleep — measured). The default 0, anything less, or a stiffness below 1e-30 pulls nothing.

members.name: Thickness
members.summary: The thickness of the spring marker's wire in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.1.

classes.name: SpringConstraint
classes.summary: A spring between the two attachments: it pulls them toward FreeLength with Stiffness force per stud of stretch (measured: k·x = m·g), slowed by Damping, within MinLength and MaxLength while LimitsEnabled.

members.name: Value
members.summary: The stored string.

classes.name: StringValue
classes.summary: A named container for one string.

members.name: CaptureFocus
members.summary: Gives this box keyboard focus, releasing any other focused box (its FocusLost fires with false).

members.name: ClearTextOnFocus
members.summary: Empties Text when the box gains focus (true by default).

members.name: FocusLost
members.summary: Fires when the box loses focus, with enterPressed: true for Return, false for Escape, a click elsewhere, or ReleaseFocus.

members.name: Focused
members.summary: Fires (with no arguments) when the box gains keyboard focus — a click or CaptureFocus.

members.name: Font
members.summary: The typed text's legacy typeface enum over FontFace (see TextLabel).

members.name: FontFace
members.summary: The typed text's typeface as a Font value (see TextLabel).

members.name: IsFocused
members.summary: Whether this box holds keyboard focus right now.

members.name: MultiLine
members.summary: Return inserts a newline instead of releasing focus.

members.name: ReleaseFocus
members.summary: Releases this box's focus; FocusLost fires with the submitted flag (false when omitted). A no-op while unfocused.

members.name: RichText
members.summary: Renders the typed Text as rich-text markup (see TextLabel).

members.name: Text
members.summary: The typed content. Keystrokes edit it while the box holds focus; writes land like any property.

members.name: TextColor3
members.summary: The typed text's color.

members.name: TextEditable
members.summary: Whether keystrokes edit Text. A non-editable box still focuses.

members.name: TextScaled
members.summary: Scales the typed text to fill the box (capped at 100 px).

members.name: TextSize
members.summary: The typed text's size in pixels, clamped to 1..100.

members.name: TextStrokeColor3
members.summary: The typed text's outline color (see TextLabel).

members.name: TextStrokeTransparency
members.summary: The typed text outline's transparency (1 by default).

members.name: TextXAlignment
members.summary: How the typed lines sit horizontally (Center by default).

members.name: TextYAlignment
members.summary: Where the typed text block sits vertically (Center by default).

classes.name: TextBox
classes.summary: Typed text input: click (or CaptureFocus) to focus, keystrokes edit Text, Enter or clicking away releases — FocusLost says which. ClearTextOnFocus, TextEditable and MultiLine behave like the reference engine; no cursor or selection yet (v1).

members.name: Font
members.summary: The label's legacy typeface enum over FontFace (see TextLabel).

members.name: FontFace

members.name: Raycast
members.summary: Casts a ray from origin along direction — the vector's length is the range. Returns a hit record (Instance, Position, Normal, Distance) or nil. The optional RaycastParams filters by both generations — FilterType over FilterDescendantsInstances, and ExcludeInstances / IncludeInstances — all applied, each entry with its descendants, RespectCanCollide skipping CanCollide-false parts; the engine also takes a plain table of the same keys (FilterType, FilterDescendantsInstances, RespectCanCollide, ServerTime). On the server under server authority, ServerTime (an engine extension: a server time in GetServerTimeNow's seconds — the one a client read from GetRenderedServerTime when it fired) tests every streamed part at the pose the server held at that time and the rest of the world live, so a shot aimed at what a client drew hits what it drew; a time older than the second the history keeps clamps to it. A client cannot pass it: it casts at the poses it draws. Validate the shot's origin against the shooter yourself, as the reference advises: the engine rewinds the targets, not the gun.

members.name: AddToFilter
members.summary: Appends an instance, or every instance of a table (nested tables too), to FilterDescendantsInstances — the old list, duplicates kept — and returns nothing; anything else is `Expected a table or Instance` (measured).

members.name: ExcludeInstances
members.summary: The newer exclusion list, nil until written and independent of FilterType's pair: a cast applies both — the listed instances and their descendants never hit, whatever IncludeInstances says. A table of instances or nil (the old list's texts for the rest); never shown by tostring and outside == (measured).

members.name: FilterDescendantsInstances
members.summary: The instances FilterType applies to, each with its logical descendants; AddToFilter appends here. A read is a fresh copy (writing into it changes nothing); a write takes a table of instances, nested tables flattened — `Invalid value type; expected a table` otherwise, `Invalid value type; table must only contain Instances and other tables` for a wrong entry. A destroyed instance stays listed while a script value names it, and filters nothing.

members.name: FilterType

members.name: IncludeInstances
members.summary: The newer inclusion list, nil until written and independent of FilterType's pair: nil admits everything, an empty list nothing, a list its instances and their descendants alone — less what ExcludeInstances and the old pair take away. A table of instances or nil; never shown by tostring and outside == (measured).

members.name: RespectCanCollide

members.name: ServerTime
members.summary: An engine extension, the server alone: a server time in Workspace:GetServerTimeNow's seconds — the one a client read from GetRenderedServerTime when it fired — at which the cast tests every streamed root at the pose the server held then, the rest of the world live. Nil (the default) casts live; a number or nil only, a non-finite one refuses at the cast, and a client's cast refuses it.

members.summary: The defaults: FilterType Exclude over an empty list, the new pair nil, the flags false, CollisionGroup "Default", ServerTime nil.

members.name: GetAsync
members.summary: The key's value and its DataStoreKeyInfo — NOTHING, zero values, for a key never written or removed (measured). Yields while the store answers. members.name: GetVersionAsync

members.decl: (key: string, delta: number?, userIds: {number}?, options: DataStoreIncrementOptions?) -> (number, DataStoreKeyInfo)
members.name: IncrementAsync
members.summary: Adds delta (1 by default, rounded to a whole number half away from zero; NaN the int32 minimum, -2147483648) to the key's number — an absent key counts from 0 — and answers the new value and its key info; a key holding anything but a number, NaN included, raises `502: … Error code: 24 Reason: Key value is not numeric.` (measured). An infinite delta raises `Unable to cast double to int` (the engine's). The options' metadata rides the write. Yields while the store answers.

members.name: ListKeysAsync
members.summary: The keys that start with prefix, sorted — a removed key too unless excludeDeleted is true (measured; false by default) — pageSize to a page (0: 50), after the cursor a key pages answered — every scope's as `<scope>/<key>` on a store opened with AllScopes; a cursor no listing answered raises `502: … Error code: 32 Reason: The provided exclusive start key is not valid.` (measured). Yields while the store answers.

members.decl: (key: string, sortDirection: Enum.SortDirection?, minDate: number?, maxDate: number?, pageSize: number?) -> DataStoreVersionPages
members.name: ListVersionsAsync
members.summary: Every version of the key — each write, a removal's marked deleted — oldest first unless sortDirection is Descending (measured), written between minDate and maxDate (Unix milliseconds, inclusive; 0 unbounded), pageSize to a page (0: 1024). Every write is kept as a version. The reference kept one version for three writes 7 s apart (measured 2026-10-16) yet two for two writes 0.3 s apart (measured 2026-10-07); the creator docs name a one-per-UTC-hour rule and a 30-day expiry, the window unmeasured. The engine merges and expires nothing. Yields while the store answers.

members.name: Parent
members.summary: The DataStoreService (measured).

members.name: RemoveAsync
members.summary: Removes the key, writing a version marked deleted, and answers the removed value and its key info; a later GetAsync answers nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

members.name: RemoveVersionAsync
members.summary: Removes one version of the key and answers nothing; the version stays listed, IsDeleted true, and GetVersionAsync of it answers nothing — the newest too, after which the key answers nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

members.decl: (key: string, value: any, userIds: {number}?, options: DataStoreSetOptions?) -> string
members.name: SetAsync
members.summary: Writes the value (and the user ids, four at most, and the options' metadata, 300 bytes at most) as a new version and answers its version id. The value is kept as JSON — a mixed table keeps its array part, a sparse array or a fractional key becomes string keys, NaN and inf survive — and refused past 4 MB of it; a function, an Instance or a Vector3 cannot be stored (`104: Cannot store <Type> in data store. …`), and a nil value raises `Argument 2 missing or nil`, storing nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

members.decl: (key: string, transform: (value: any, keyInfo: DataStoreKeyInfo?) -> (any, {number}?, {[string]: any}?)) -> (any, DataStoreKeyInfo)
members.name: UpdateAsync
members.summary: Calls transform with the key's value and key info (nil, nil for a key with none) and stores what it returns — the value, the user ids, the metadata — answering the stored value and its key info; a transform returning nil writes nothing and the call answers one nil. A transform that yields (inside a pcall too) or errors is logged (`Transform function error Callbacks cannot yield`; the error with its stack, then `Transform function error <message>`) and the call answers nothing and raises nothing — the value stays; a yielded transform runs on when its wait wakes, its result discarded (measured). If the key changed under the transform, it runs again on the new value. Yields while the store answers.

members.name: BindToRenderStep
members.summary: Client only: runs callback every frame in the render step, before RenderStepped, in ascending priority (Enum.RenderPriority values; bind order among equals), with the frame's delta time. Binding a name again adds a second binding, each running at its own priority (measured) — unbind before rebinding. A binding ends with UnbindFromRenderStep or the script. members.decl: (callback: (deltaTime: number) -> (), frequency: Enum.StepFrequency?, priority: number?) -> BVScriptConnection
members.name: BindToSimulation
members.summary: Runs callback inside the fixed simulation loop, once per step its frequency divides (Hz30 by default: every second 60 Hz step — the simulation tick; Hz60 every step, down to Hz1), ahead of that step's physics, on the server and the client alike, in ascending priority (2000 by default; bind order among equals). deltaTime is the frequency's period exactly (1/30 for Hz30). A write here is what the step simulates. The returned connection is the unbind; a binding also ends with its script.

members.name: GetPredictionStatus
members.summary: What instance is to this end: Authoritative on the server, Predicted on a client that predicts it under server authority, None otherwise (the classic rules apply). Readable inside a BindToSimulation callback, so one bound module can run on both ends and skip what neither end simulates.

members.name: GetRenderedSessionTick
members.summary: The session tick, fractional, this frame draws at (an engine extension, GetSessionTick's counterpart for what is on screen): what a script reads to draw something that is a function of the tick — a scrolling track, a conveyor's marks — where the things beside it are drawn. With no instance, this end's own simulation: the server's and solo play's world, a client's predicted instances and what its own scripts made. Under server authority a mover written at the tick is shown one tick behind and eased across it, so the answer is GetSessionTick() - 1 plus the frame's phase through the tick; it runs on whether or not such an instance exists, so what is drawn from it never jumps when one stops or is gone, and a tick the session's numbering catches up or holds on a poor link is spread over the frames after it, as the bodies are shown. With an instance, where that instance is drawn (a welded part through its assembly's root): one this end simulates answers as above; a followed one is drawn at its playback's position — the tick the server's own snapshots give it, behind the server's present by the link and the playback's depth, running on while it rests; one the server moves that this end plays nothing back of answers with the followed world's median. Under the classic model nothing is eased across ticks (this end's own simulation answers GetSessionTick()) and poses carry no tick (a followed instance answers from the numbering, within a tick). -1 on a client before its numbering aligned.

members.name: GetSessionTick
members.summary: The simulation tick this end stands at, numbered as the session numbers it (an engine extension; the reference has no tick API): the server's own count on the server and in solo play, on a client the server tick its fixed loop is at — its lead ahead of the server included, so an input consumed at tick N is applied by the server at its tick N. Inside a BindToSimulation callback the tick being simulated. -1 on a client before its numbering aligned. A game stamps its own remotes with it, so the other end knows the tick an action happened on.

A name or scope is 1 to 50 characters (`DataStore name can't be empty string`, `DataStore name is too long`, `DataStore scope can't be empty string`, `DataStore scope is too long`); a number is its text. members.name: PublishAsync
members.summary: Sends message to every subscriber of topic on this server: the value travels as JSON text (HttpService's codec, 1 KiB at most — `MessagingService:PublishAsync(): Cannot publish, data exceeded 1kb`) and arrives on a later frame as one table { Data, Sent }: a copy of the value and the session clock's Unix seconds at the publish (GetServerTimeNow's). A topic is 1 to 80 characters (`MessagingService: Topic names cannot be empty.`, `MessagingService: Topic names cannot be more than 80 characters.`). One server only: no other server receives it. The server's alone — a client side's call raises `MessagingService can only be executed by game server`.

members.decl: (topic: string, callback: (message: { Data: any, Sent: number }) -> ()) -> BVScriptConnection
members.name: SubscribeAsync
members.summary: Calls callback with every message published to topic on this server from now on — a table { Data, Sent } of its own per publish, the newest subscriber first, on a frame after it — and answers the connection: Disconnect stops the deliveries, and the script's end takes them with it. The topic is refused as PublishAsync's (empty, past 80 characters). The server's alone — a client side's call raises `MessagingService can only be executed by game server`.

services.name: MessagingService
services.summary: Topic messages within this server: SubscribeAsync connects a callback to a topic, PublishAsync sends a value to its subscribers, delivered on a later frame as one table { Data, Sent }. The engine runs one server per game, so a publish reaches no other server, and the reference's per-minute limits are not kept. The server's alone: a client side's call raises.
